This may seem like some distant political science fiction novel to you, but the Founders had this general type of scenario in mind when they added the 2nd amendment. The 2nd amendment was included in the Bill of Rights to provide a final, ultimate check on the potential abuse of federal power – but not as the first response. There are a whole host of legal, constitutional, and peaceful measures that can be taken before the 2nd amendment comes into play – but it must be understood that the 2nd amendment is not primarily about personal self-defense or the right to hunt or target shoot. It was included to preserve a balance of power between the federal government and the people – i.e., to ensure that the people would retain the ultimate ability to enforce their will upon the federal government if it ever became a rogue government.
